method: classify (Xlog gc,safepoint closed-loop) then measure CO-free (open-loop wrk2 fixed -R)

step1_classifier.conclusion: max GC pause (23-28ms) << closed-loop max (128-148ms); 0 full GCs; heap 256->768 leaves tail+p99 unchanged (only minor-GC count drops). 'exeris lean-heap GC-tail' falsified in a 2nd regime (light/closed-loop/SMT-sat) alongside §7 heavy/open-loop.

step2_openloop_cofree.note: open-loop wrk2, attained ~= offered (CO-free true service time). Closed-loop max was CO-inflated AND backwards.

findings: Closed-loop reading was BACKWARDS: CO-free, exeris has the TIGHTEST tail (p99.9 2.36ms, max 25.6ms @30k; still tight at 48k near saturation).
Exeris extreme tail (~22ms p99.999) = the occasional young-GC pause (matches Step 1); benign, heap-independent. No 3am problem in exeris; closed-loop 148ms was CO amplification.
quarkus-tuned 913ms p99.9 here is a SINGLE-EVENT OUTLIER, contradicted by §7 (12.22ms at the same 30k rung, n=2). NOT a quarkus tail claim.
quarkus-hibernate comparable to exeris here (p99.9 4.38ms, max 35.7ms); better than §7's co-resident 19.91ms, consistent with §7's co-residence thesis.

section7_cross_validation.key_discovery: §7 recorded latency_p999_us in every leaf but published p99 only; mining p99.9 strengthens §7's own light conclusion.
section7_cross_validation.new_result: At p99.9 exeris is FLAT 1.94-2.60ms while both quarkus arms run 3-8x higher across the ENTIRE ladder (from 6k), whereas §7's published p99 shows separation only at 24-30k. §7 under-states its own light result.
section7_cross_validation.extends_s7: This run adds a 48k rung (past §7's 30k top): exeris p99.9 4.12ms - flatness holds to 84% of its ceiling.
section7_cross_validation.contradicts_this_run: quarkus-tuned @30k: §7 p99.9 = 12.22ms (n=2) vs this run 913ms (n=1) -> outlier.
section7_cross_validation.heavy_context: §7 heavy p99.9 @10k: exeris 37.3 (pair-1) / 40.4 (pair-2) vs quarkus-tuned 13.8; hibernate pair-3 99.7 vs pair-2 31.3 reproduces the 'heavier neighbor -> fatter tail' signature. Consistent with §7's co-residence reading.

outlier_arithmetic: At 30k rps x 300s = 9M requests, ONE ~1s stall delays every request scheduled during it (~30k = 0.33% > 0.1%), alone driving p99.9 -> ~913ms and p99.99/max -> ~1.0s. Signature of one event in one window; §7's 120s windows are less likely to catch it.
caveats: Loopback; fair across stacks, not transferable to real network.
Open-loop rungs sub-saturation (attained ~= offered) => percentiles are true service time; closed-loop max used only as the initiating smoke alarm.

quarkus-tuned 1.02s is n=1 AND contradicted by §7 (12.22ms same rung): single-event outlier, not a property. Do not publish as a quarkus tail claim. To settle frequency: repeat @30k x3, longer windows, -Xlog:gc,safepoint + pool/timeout logging.

This run is truly single-target (verified: one target-app per run, no co-locator) - the isolated reference §7's pairwise harness could not provide. Levels not directly comparable to §7's co-resident leaves; ordering and exeris absolutes agree.
